👋 Welcome to Morrow

#getting-started

Morrow is a calm place to write, plan and keep what you know. There is no account, no subscription, no AI and no ads, and nothing you write is ever sent anywhere. Every page is a plain Markdown file in a folder you chose, so your notes stay yours even without Morrow.

How to use this guide

Each chapter below is a real page that shows its feature working. Try things, change them, break them. When you are done, delete this page from its ••• menu at the top right and every chapter and example goes with it.

Start in five minutes

  1. Press Alt N (⌥ N on a Mac) to make a page. Give it a title and press Enter.

  2. Type / on an empty line to pick any block: headings, checklists, tables, columns, databases and more.

  3. Type [[ to link to another page, and @ to mention a date like @tomorrow.

  4. Press Alt D to open today’s note, a page for every day that collects what happened.

  5. Press Ctrl K (⌘ K) to search everything and run any command by name.

Why Morrow

  • Your files, forever. Pages are Markdown, canvases are JSON Canvas, databases are folders of pages. Open them in any text editor.

  • Powerful databases, offline. Databases with board, table, calendar, list and gallery views, relations and formulas, all on your own computer.

  • Everything built in. Links, backlinks, a graph, canvases and daily notes work the moment you open the app. No plugins to hunt for.

  • Private by design. No telemetry, no cloud, no AI reading your notes. Lock any page with a password, sync between your own devices over your own network.

  • Free and open source. No plans, no seats, no paywalled features. Ever.

Daily notes

Press Alt D or click Today in the sidebar. Each day gets its own page inside a Journal page, newest first. Use it as a diary, a work log, or the place where everything lands before it finds a home.

Tasks

Any checklist item on any page is a task. Tasks in the sidebar gathers every open one, grouped by page. Give a task a date with @:

  • Water the tomatoes Oct 20, 2026

  • Send the draft Oct 22, 2026

  • Read the welcome guide Oct 19, 2026

Quick capture

Press Ctrl Alt M (⌘ ⌥ M) from any app, even with Morrow in the background. Type a thought and it goes into today’s note without leaving what you were doing.

Templates

  1. Make a page the way you like it, for example a meeting note with headings for agenda, notes and actions.

  2. Choose Save as template from its ••• menu. It is copied into a Templates page.

  3. Press Alt T to make a new page from any template.

  4. A template called Daily note is used for every new daily note.

Templates can use {{date}}, {{time}} and {{title}}, which are filled in when the page is made.

🔒 Privacy, history and encryption

#getting-started

Nothing leaves your computer

Morrow has no servers. It never phones home, has no analytics and no AI. The only time it uses the network is when you ask it to: loading a picture from the web, or syncing with your own devices.

Your vault

Your notes live in a vault, a normal folder. Open it from the vault menu at the top of the sidebar, or with Show in folder in a page’s menu. You can edit the files in any app while Morrow is open and it follows along. Keep the folder in a backup or a synced drive if you like.

Page history

Morrow keeps earlier versions of a page as you work. Choose Page history from the page menu to see what changed, line by line, and bring back any version.

Password protected pages

  1. Choose Encrypt with a password from a page’s menu.

  2. The file on disk becomes unreadable without the password, using AES-256.

  3. Unlock it with the password when you open it, and lock it again from the menu.

There is no way back

If you forget the password, nobody can open the page. Not you, and not Morrow.

Trash

Deleted pages go to the Trash in the sidebar first, so a slip is never permanent.

🔄 Sync, import, export and publishing

#getting-started

Sync between your devices

Open Settings and turn on sync on two computers on the same network. Pair them once with the code one of them shows, and from then on they keep each other up to date directly, with no cloud in between. When both change the same page, both versions are kept so nothing is lost.

You can also put the vault folder in any sync service you already trust, such as a synced cloud drive.

Bring your notes in

  • From other note apps: export your workspace as Markdown and CSV, then choose the zip in Import. Databases come across as databases.

  • From a folder of Markdown notes: open it as a Morrow vault. Wiki links, tags, callouts and canvases already work.

  • Markdown files and folders from anywhere else, and CSV files as databases.

Take them out

  • Export as Markdown saves a page with its attachments.

  • Export as PDF saves the page as it looks, ready to print or send.

  • Or just copy the vault folder. It already is your export.

Publish a website

Choose Publish as a website from a page’s menu to turn it and its subpages into a small static site, with navigation and working links. Upload the folder to any static web host.

  4. Press Alt D to open today’s note, a page for every day that collects what happened.

🔗 Links, tags and the graph

#getting-started

Notes become more useful the more they are connected. Morrow makes connecting them quick.

Links

  • Type [[ and pick a page to link it: Databases.

  • Show different words for a link with [[Page|words]]: the whiteboard chapter.

  • A link to a page that does not exist yet, like An idea for later, is shown faded. Click it and the page is made.

  • Hold Ctrl (⌘) while clicking a link to open it in a new tab.

Backlinks and mentions

At the bottom of every page is a list of the pages that link to it, with the sentence each link sits in. Below that, unlinked mentions finds pages that name this page without linking it, and opens each one right at the mention so you can link it.

Dates

Type @ to mention a date: Oct 19, 2026, Oct 20, 2026 or Oct 26, 2026. Click one to open that day’s note. In the file it is a link like [[2026-10-19]], the common way daily notes are named.

Tags

Write a tag anywhere in text, like #ideas or #reading/fiction, or add tags under the title of a page. Tags in the sidebar lists every tag and the pages that use it. Click a tag to see them all.

The graph

Press Alt G for the graph: every page is a dot and every link a line. Drag dots around, zoom with the wheel, and click one to open it. Open the graph from a page’s menu to see only what is near that page.

📅 Daily notes, tasks and templates

#getting-started

Daily notes

Press Alt D or click Today in the sidebar. Each day gets its own page inside a Journal page, newest first. Use it as a diary, a work log, or the place where everything lands before it finds a home.

Tasks

Any checklist item on any page is a task. Tasks in the sidebar gathers every open one, grouped by page. Give a task a date with @:

  • Water the tomatoes Oct 20, 2026

  • Send the draft Oct 22, 2026

  • Read the welcome guide Oct 19, 2026

Quick capture

Press Ctrl Alt M (⌘ ⌥ M) from any app, even with Morrow in the background. Type a thought and it goes into today’s note without leaving what you were doing.

Templates

  1. Make a page the way you like it, for example a meeting note with headings for agenda, notes and actions.

  2. Choose Save as template from its ••• menu. It is copied into a Templates page.

  3. Press Alt T to make a new page from any template.

  4. A template called Daily note is used for every new daily note.

Templates can use {{date}}, {{time}} and {{title}}, which are filled in when the page is made.

🗃️ Databases

#getting-started

A database is a page whose subpages are its rows. Each row is a full page with its own content, plus properties like status, dates and numbers. In your vault a database is a folder, and each row is a Markdown file with its properties at the top, readable by any Markdown app.

An example

Here is the Reading list, shown right inside this page. Drag cards between columns, click one to open it, and switch views with the tabs:

Reading list

Views

View Good for
Table Seeing and editing every property at once
Board Moving things through stages, grouped by a select
Calendar Anything with a date, drag rows between days
List A quiet list of titles
Gallery Cards with the first picture of each page as a cover

Each view keeps its own filters, sorts, grouping and hidden properties. Add one with the + next to the view tabs.

Properties

Type Holds
Text, Number, Link Words, amounts, web addresses
Select, Multi-select One or more coloured choices
Date, Checkbox A day, yes or no
Relation Links to other pages, written as [[links]] in the file
Formula A value worked out from the other properties

Formulas look like prop("Pages") * 2 or if(prop("Status") == "Finished", "done", "not yet"). Open a formula property from its column header to see every function, with examples.

Make one

  • Type /database for a database on its own page, or /inline database for one shown inside the page you are on.

  • Or click + next to Pages in the sidebar and choose Database.

  • Import a CSV file from Import to turn a spreadsheet into a database.

🔒 Privacy, history and encryption

#getting-started

Nothing leaves your computer

Morrow has no servers. It never phones home, has no analytics and no AI. The only time it uses the network is when you ask it to: loading a picture from the web, or syncing with your own devices.

Your vault

Your notes live in a vault, a normal folder. Open it from the vault menu at the top of the sidebar, or with Show in folder in a page’s menu. You can edit the files in any app while Morrow is open and it follows along. Keep the folder in a backup or a synced drive if you like.

Page history

Morrow keeps earlier versions of a page as you work. Choose Page history from the page menu to see what changed, line by line, and bring back any version.

Password protected pages

  1. Choose Encrypt with a password from a page’s menu.

  2. The file on disk becomes unreadable without the password, using AES-256.

  3. Unlock it with the password when you open it, and lock it again from the menu.

There is no way back

If you forget the password, nobody can open the page. Not you, and not Morrow.

Trash

Deleted pages go to the Trash in the sidebar first, so a slip is never permanent.

🔄 Sync, import, export and publishing

#getting-started

Sync between your devices

Open Settings and turn on sync on two computers on the same network. Pair them once with the code one of them shows, and from then on they keep each other up to date directly, with no cloud in between. When both change the same page, both versions are kept so nothing is lost.

You can also put the vault folder in any sync service you already trust, such as a synced cloud drive.

Bring your notes in

  • From other note apps: export your workspace as Markdown and CSV, then choose the zip in Import. Databases come across as databases.

  • From a folder of Markdown notes: open it as a Morrow vault. Wiki links, tags, callouts and canvases already work.

  • Markdown files and folders from anywhere else, and CSV files as databases.

Take them out

  • Export as Markdown saves a page with its attachments.

  • Export as PDF saves the page as it looks, ready to print or send.

  • Or just copy the vault folder. It already is your export.

Publish a website

Choose Publish as a website from a page’s menu to turn it and its subpages into a small static site, with navigation and working links. Upload the folder to any static web host.

⚙️ Make it yours

#getting-started

Look and feel

In Settings (Ctrl ,) choose:

  • Light, dark or the same as your system. Ctrl Shift L switches.

  • An accent colour, and whether headings, lists and tags are colourful.

  • A sans, serif or mono font for writing, and a comfortable or wide page.

Icons and covers

Hover over a page title for Add icon and Add cover. Icons come from a full emoji picker with search. Covers are colour gradients or any picture from your computer.

Tabs

  • Ctrl T opens a new tab and Ctrl W closes it. Ctrl Tab moves between them.

  • Ctrl click, or middle click, any page in the sidebar or any link to open it in a new tab.

  • Drag tabs to reorder them. They are remembered when you come back.

The sidebar

  • Drag pages to reorder them or to put one inside another.

  • Right click a page for its menu, or star it to keep it in Favourites.

  • Ctrl \ hides the sidebar and drag its edge to resize it.

Custom CSS

Restyle anything from Settings, under Custom CSS. It is saved in your vault as .morrow/style.css and travels with your notes. For example:

:root {
  --accent: #e5484d;
}
.page-title {
  letter-spacing: -0.03em;
}

That is everything. Delete this guide whenever you are ready, and make Morrow yours.
